operator_io_quirks: Tiny DB: body_builder 5 rows, people 6 rows; original_values lists are short (<=6), so rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) nearly exhausts them.
FK body_builder.People_ID -> people.People_ID exists and is unique (people PK); no dangling FK, no self-FK, no composite PK.
All columns notnull=0 and null_rate=0.0: no NULLs in original, but NOT NULL is not declared, so TS may emit NULLs freely.
Birth_Date is TEXT storing 'January 1, 1992' style (month-name, comma, space); declared type TEXT dispatches to String fuzzer, NOT Date.
Birth_Place is TEXT 'City, State' with comma+space; String fuzzer will not reproduce the comma pattern.
Name is TEXT 'First Last' with a space; String fuzzer charset includes space so plausible-ish but random.
All numeric columns are REAL storage with .0/.5 values; declared INT for IDs but storage integer — consistent here.
Snatch/Clean_Jerk/Total are REAL with 1-decimal values; Number fuzzer scale=4 will emit 4-decimal floats, contradicting the .5 granularity.
Total = Snatch + Clean_Jerk in original (arithmetic invariant) but no CHECK constraint declares it.
Table/column names are mixed case (Body_Builder_ID, Clean_Jerk) — must be double-quoted; column lookup case-insensitive.
DDL uses backtick-quoted `people` in the FK clause — sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim for the clone.
No indexes, views, or triggers beyond the two CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer (scale=4) on Body_Builder_ID/People_ID: uniform in [-10^4,10^4] then +-1/+-2 perturbation -> huge IDs, implausible vs 1..6.
Number fuzzer on Snatch/Clean_Jerk/Total: 4-decimal floats in [-10^4,10^4] -> negative weights, values far from 130-180 kg range.
String fuzzer on Name: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, contaminated 50% -> not 'First Last' shape; FN on name-pattern queries.
String fuzzer on Birth_Date: random strings, never 'Month D, YYYY' -> any date-format query (strftime, LIKE '%1992%') gets FN.
String fuzzer on Birth_Place: random strings, no 'City, State' comma -> LIKE '%,%' queries FN.
FK fill: body_builder.People_ID drawn from people.People_ID final values with replacement -> duplicates allowed, so join cardinality differs from 1:1 original.
PK drop: Body_Builder_ID/People_ID PK duplicates dropped, so table sizes shrink below chosen size; small tables (<=2500) mean many collisions.
No NOT NULL/CHECK enforcement in Python: NULLs and negative values inserted fine; only PK/unique/FK-at-insert would fail (FK pragma OFF).
Total not tied to Snatch+Clean_Jerk -> queries asserting Total=Snatch+Clean_Jerk get FN.
Height/Weight REAL: 4-decimal random in [-10^4,10^4] -> negative heights, implausible; range queries (Height>200) get FP/FN.
Small original (6 rows) means original_values sampling is nearly deterministic; literal pool from train SQL dominates element set.
Birth_Date as String means TS never uses Date fuzzer here — a known TS miss for text-stored dates.
